subject_offered_latest_by_section.name: subject_offered_latest_by_section
subject_offered_latest_by_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY,
  TERM_CODE,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_SORT,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_DESC,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  COURSE_NUMBER,
  COURSE_NUMBER_SORT,
  COURSE_NUMBER_DESC,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  SECTION_ID,
  IS_MASTER_SECTION,
  IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  IS_LAB_SECTION,
  IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  IS_DESIGN_SECTION,
  OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  MEET_TIME,
  MEET_PLACE,
  CLUSTER_TYPE,
  CLUSTER_TYPE_DESC,
  CLUSTER_LIST,
  HGN_CODE,
  HGN_CODE_DESC,
  FORM_TYPE,
  FORM_TYPE_DESC,
  SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  SECTION_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  EVALUATE_THIS_SUBJECT,
  IS_OSE_SUBJECT,
  IS_CREATED_BY_DATA_WAREHOUSE,
  SUBJECT_GROUPING_KEY,
  WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  IS_REPEATABLE_SUBJECT,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY SECTION_ID
    ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '') DESC, SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY DESC
  ) AS section_row_rank
FROM subject_offered

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumer can filter where section_row_rank = 1 to get latest per SECTION_ID

subject_offered_latest_by_section.description: For each SECTION_ID in subject_offered, pick the latest SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY row by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE. Useful when downstream queries need one canonical/latest record per section (top-K by recency). | Use for: Get latest section offerings and their enrollment counts; De-duplicate multiple records per section by latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE; Join latest section row to faculty or room tables

subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.name: subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.body_sql:
SELECT
  TERM_CODE,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  SCHOOL_CODE,
  SCHOOL_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_cluster_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_credit,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_listen,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_first_week,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week,
  MAX(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS last_warehouse_load_date
FROM subject_summary
GROUP BY
  TERM_CODE,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  SCHOOL_CODE,
  SCHOOL_NAME

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers can restrict by TERM_CODE or SCHOOL_CODE

params.description: Aggregated enrollment and credit/listen counts per academic term and subject (subject-level totals within a term).
params.when_to_use: Get total enrollments, credits, and first-/fifth-week counts for a specific subject in a specific term. | Compare enrollment or credit volume across subjects within the same term. | Drive dashboards or reports that show term-by-term subject-level enrollment and credit aggregates. | Use as a pre-aggregated input when computing higher-level summaries (department, school, or term totals) without double-counting.
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: academic term identifier (from subject_summary.TERM_CODE) | SUBJECT_ID: subject code/identifier (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID) | SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sortable subject identifier used for ordering (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT) | SUBJECT_TITLE: human-readable subject title (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE) | MASTER_SUBJECT_ID: master/normalized subject id for grouping variants (from subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) | MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sortable master subject id (from subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT) | DEPARTMENT_CODE: department code owning the subject (from subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_CODE) | DEPARTMENT_NAME: department display name (from subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_NAME) | SCHOOL_CODE: school code that contains the department (from subject_summary.SCHOOL_CODE) | SCHOOL_NAME: school display name (from subject_summary.SCHOOL_NAME) | total_subject_enrollment_number: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_cluster_enrollment_number: sum of CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_credit: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_listen: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_first_week: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | last_warehouse_load_date: most recent WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE among underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE aggregated with MAX(...))
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_CODE | subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_NAME | subject_summary.SCHOOL_CODE | subject_summary.SCHOOL_NAME | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: total_subject_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_cluster_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_credit = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_listen = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_first_week = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | last_warehouse_load_date = MAX(subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) GROUPED BY the same grouping columns
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a term dimension (e.g., time_month_fiscal_anchor) on TERM_CODE — safe because this view is one row per TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID (joining on TERM_CODE alone will not duplicate the view's subject-level measures if you preserve the subject-level rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a subject/dimension lookup that is one-row-per-SUBJECT_ID (or per MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) — safe because the lookup is expected to be 1:1 to SUBJECT_ID (or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) and will not duplicate aggregated measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail-level tables or views (for example: subject_offered_latest_by_section or any section-level table) without re-aggregating that detail to the same grain (TERM_CODE + SUBJECT_ID or the appropriate grouping) first, because those joins would multiply this view's measures. If you must join to subject_offered_latest_by_section, first aggregate that view to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID (e.g., SUM or COUNT per TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID) and then join — or join on both TERM_CODE and SECTION-unique keys while selecting non-aggregated attributes carefully. | do NOT join to fac_rooms_space_area or other room-level one-to-many tables without aggregation, since each room/space row can replicate the subject-level totals. | when rolling up to department- or school-level totals, aggregate these metrics (SUM of total_subject_enrollment_* grouped by DEPARTMENT_CODE or SCHOOL_CODE). Because this view is already aggregated at subject x term grain, summing its metric columns by department or school yields correct higher-level totals. | if joining to sibling views that have different grains or ranking logic (e.g., subject_offered_latest_by_section(RANK)), ensure you either: (a) aggregate the sibling to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID before joining, or (b) join on unique keys that guarantee 1:1. Otherwise re-aggregate after the join to restore correct totals.

subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.description: Aggregates enrollment and unit measures from subject_summary by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID. One row per combination of TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID with common measures exposed for reporting trend and joins. | Use for: Term-by-term enrollment trends for a subject; Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment by subject; Join aggregated subject enrollment to department or faculty tables

fac_rooms_space_area.name: fac_rooms_space_area
fac_rooms_space_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  ff.FLOOR_KEY AS FLOOR_KEY,
  fr.ROOM,
  fr.SPACE_ID,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_KEY,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.USE_KEY,
  fr.USE_DESC,
  fr.MINOR_USE_KEY,
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION,
  fr.AREA,
  fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  fr.DEPT_CODE,
  fr.ACCESS_LEVEL,
  fr.LATITUDE_WGS,
  fr.LONGITUDE_WGS,
  fr.NORTHING_SPCS,
  fr.EASTING_SPCS,
  fr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM fac_rooms fr
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers can filter by AREA or ORGANIZATION_KEY

params.description: Provides one-row-per-room facility space attributes and area for rooms (fac_rooms) enriched with building and floor lookup attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get room-level attributes and area for reporting or analytics (e.g., list rooms with area, location, use, and organization). | Filter or aggregate total area by building, floor, use, or organization (use this view as the grain of FAC_ROOM_KEY and then aggregate). | Join room-level spatial attributes (latitude/longitude, easting/northing) to other datasets at room granularity. | Serve as the base for composing higher-level facility metrics (building- or floor-level area aggregations) by aggregating AREA grouped by BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY.
params.output_schema: FAC_ROOM_KEY: surrogate key for the room at the grain of this view; derived from fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY (fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY). | BUILDING_KEY: foreign key to the building; derived from fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY (fr.BUILDING_KEY). | BUILDING_NAME: descriptive name of the building; derived from fac_building.BUILDING_NAME (fb.BUILDING_NAME) via left join on BUILDING_KEY = FAC_BUILDING_KEY. | BUILDING_NUMBER: building number/code; derived from fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER (fb.BUILDING_NUMBER). | FLOOR: human floor label stored on the room record; derived from fac_rooms.FLOOR (fr.FLOOR). | FLOOR_KEY: floor surrogate key; derived from fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY (ff.FLOOR_KEY) via left join on fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY. | ROOM: room identifier (room number or name within floor); derived from fac_rooms.ROOM (fr.ROOM). | SPACE_ID: alternative space identifier from fac_rooms; derived from fac_rooms.SPACE_ID (fr.SPACE_ID). | MAJOR_USE_KEY: code for major use category for the room; derived from fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_KEY (fr.MAJOR_USE_KEY). | MAJOR_USE_DESC: description of the major use; derived from fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC (fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC). | USE_KEY: code for use classification; derived from fac_rooms.USE_KEY (fr.USE_KEY). | USE_DESC: description of the use classification; derived from fac_rooms.USE_DESC (fr.USE_DESC). | MINOR_USE_KEY: finer-grained use code; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_KEY (fr.MINOR_USE_KEY). | MINOR_USE_DESC: description of the minor use; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_DESC (fr.MINOR_USE_DESC). | ORGANIZATION_KEY: owning/assigned organization key for the room; derived from fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY (fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY). | ORGANIZATION_NAME: organization name assigned to the room; derived from fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME (fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME). | MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY: subordinate organization key; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY (fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY). | MINOR_ORGANIZATION: subordinate organization name; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION (fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION). | AREA: numeric area measure for the room (same units as source); derived from fac_rooms.AREA (fr.AREA). | ROOM_FULL_NAME: full descriptive room name; derived from fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME (fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME). | DEPT_CODE: department code associated with the room; derived from fac_rooms.DEPT_CODE (fr.DEPT_CODE). | ACCESS_LEVEL: access/security level for the room; derived from fac_rooms.ACCESS_LEVEL (fr.ACCESS_LEVEL). | LATITUDE_WGS: latitude (WGS84) for room location; derived from fac_rooms.LATITUDE_WGS (fr.LATITUDE_WGS). | LONGITUDE_WGS: longitude (WGS84) for room location; derived from fac_rooms.LONGITUDE_WGS (fr.LONGITUDE_WGS). | NORTHING_SPCS: projected northing coordinate (state plane or similar) for room; derived from fac_rooms.NORTHING_SPCS (fr.NORTHING_SPCS). | EASTING_SPCS: projected easting coordinate for room; derived from fac_rooms.EASTING_SPCS (fr.EASTING_SPCS). | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: data warehouse load timestamp for the room row; derived from fac_rooms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE (fr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE).
params.grounded_columns: fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY | fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY | fac_building.BUILDING_NAME | fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | fac_rooms.FLOOR | fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY | fac_rooms.ROOM | fac_rooms.SPACE_ID | fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_KEY | fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC | fac_rooms.USE_KEY | fac_rooms.USE_DESC | fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_KEY | fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_DESC | fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY | fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME | fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY | fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION | fac_rooms.AREA | fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME | fac_rooms.DEPT_CODE | fac_rooms.ACCESS_LEVEL | fac_rooms.LATITUDE_WGS | fac_rooms.LONGITUDE_WGS | fac_rooms.NORTHING_SPCS | fac_rooms.EASTING_SPCS | fac_rooms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: AREA = fac_rooms.AREA  -- atomic numeric measure at the FAC_ROOM_KEY grain; no aggregation applied in the view (consumers must aggregate AREA when rolling up).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to building-level or floor-level dimension views (e.g., fac_building or fac_floor) on BUILDING_KEY = fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY = fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY is safe because this view is one-row-per FAC_ROOM_KEY and the fac_building and fac_floor side are one-row-per-building / one-row-per-floor. Those joins do not duplicate AREA. | cardinality-SAFE: join to time or fiscal anchor dimensions (e.g., time_month_fiscal_anchor) on unrelated time keys is safe provided you do not cross-multiply rows; such joins should be done only when you are attaching a single time value per room (e.g., WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE -> month). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many fact/detail tables (e.g., event logs, bookings, or enrollments) without pre-aggregating the many-side to the FAC_ROOM_KEY grain first or using distinct/aggregation after join, because such joins will multiply room rows and therefore over-count AREA. | do NOT join to sibling aggregation views that are multi-row-per-room (if any) without ensuring a one-to-one mapping or aggregating back to FAC_ROOM_KEY, because AREA is stored at room grain and will be duplicated if the join outputs multiple rows per FAC_ROOM_KEY. | When composing higher-level metrics: compute building- or floor-level area by aggregating AREA grouped by BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY from this view (e.g., SUM(AREA) GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY). This preserves correct cardinality. | If you need to attach many-side details (e.g., room bookings): either (a) aggregate the many-side to FAC_ROOM_KEY first and then join one-to-one, or (b) join and then re-aggregate using SUM(AREA) OVER (GROUP BY ...) carefully to avoid multiplication.

fac_rooms_space_area.description: Denormalized room-level space data joining fac_rooms to fac_building and fac_floor where available. One row per FAC_ROOM_KEY with building and floor attributes to support spatial reporting and allocations. | Use for: Room area by department/building for space utilization; Map rooms with coordinates; Aggregate area by building or organization

employee_directory_contact_normalized.name: employee_directory_contact_normalized
employee_directory_contact_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  MIT_ID,
  LAST_NAME,
  FIRST_NAME,
  MIDDLE_NAME,
  FULL_NAME,
  DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME,
  OFFICE_LOCATION,
  OFFICE_PHONE,
  DIRECTORY_TITLE,
  PRIMARY_TITLE,
  DEPARTMENT_NUMBER,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  KRB_NAME,
  KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE,
  EMAIL_ADDRESS,

  NAME_KNOWN_BY,

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers may restrict to IS_ACTIVE variants in other tables

params.description: Provides one-row-per-person (MIT_ID) normalized contact and name information from the employee_directory table.
params.when_to_use: Look up contact details (email, phone, office) and canonical/preferred names for a single employee or a set of employees. | Join person contact/name info onto other datasets by MIT_ID to annotate records with directory attributes (department, title, kerb, URLs). | Compose reports or downstream views that need stable person-level identifiers and preferred-name fallbacks (e.g., display name logic). | Filter or group other fact-level data by department, primary title, or kerb name after joining on MIT_ID.
params.output_schema: MIT_ID: Unique person identifier (base column employee_directory.MIT_ID). | LAST_NAME: Family/last name as stored (employee_directory.LAST_NAME). | FIRST_NAME: Given/first name as stored (employee_directory.FIRST_NAME). | MIDDLE_NAME: Middle name as stored (employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME). | FULL_NAME: Full name field from directory (employee_directory.FULL_NAME). | DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME: Full name as shown in the directory (employee_directory.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME). | OFFICE_LOCATION: Office building/room location (employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION). | OFFICE_PHONE: Office phone number (employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE). | DIRECTORY_TITLE: Title as shown in directory (employee_directory.DIRECTORY_TITLE). | PRIMARY_TITLE: Primary job title (employee_directory.PRIMARY_TITLE). | DEPARTMENT_NUMBER: Department numeric/code (employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER). | DEPARTMENT_NAME: Department name (employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NAME). | KRB_NAME: Kerberos username (employee_directory.KRB_NAME). | KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE: Kerberos username uppercased (employee_directory.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE). | EMAIL_ADDRESS: Email address (employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS). | PERSONAL_URL: Personal or profile URL (employee_directory.PERSONAL_URL). | NAME_KNOWN_BY: Alternate known-as name(s) (employee_directory.NAME_KNOWN_BY). | EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE: Uppercased email address (employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE). | FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE: Uppercased full name (employee_directory.FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE). | PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME: Preferred first name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME, employee_directory.FIRST_NAME). | PREFERRED_LAST_NAME: Preferred last name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME, employee_directory.LAST_NAME). | PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME: Preferred middle name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME, employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME).
params.grounded_columns: employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.DIRECTORY_TITLE | employee_directory.PRIMARY_TITLE | employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER | employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NAME | employee_directory.KRB_NAME | employee_directory.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS | employee_directory.PERSONAL_URL | employee_directory.NAME_KNOWN_BY | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME | employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME
params.metric: PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME, employee_directory.FIRST_NAME) | PREFERRED_LAST_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME, employee_directory.LAST_NAME) | PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME, employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to person- or identity-keyed dimensions (one-row-per-MIT_ID) on MIT_ID — safe because this view is one-row-per-MIT_ID and joining to another one-row-per-MIT_ID object does not duplicate rows. Example: join to another person view keyed by MIT_ID. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables (for example: events, course sections, or any enrollment/attendance table keyed by MIT_ID with multiple rows per person) without aggregation on the many side first, because those joins will multiply this view's rows and duplicate person-level attributes. Instead aggregate or deduplicate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(*) per MIT_ID) before joining. | safe composition with sibling views: you may join on MIT_ID to other views that explicitly declare one-row-per-MIT_ID. Do NOT assume sibling views listed (subject_offered_latest_by_section, subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject, fac_rooms_space_area, time_month_fiscal_anchor) are one-row-per-MIT_ID — inspect their grain. For example, joining to subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject (AGG) is unsafe unless that AGG is pre-aggregated to MIT_ID, because it is aggregated by term/subject, not by MIT_ID. | when joining to departmental or organizational dimensions by DEPARTMENT_NUMBER or DEPARTMENT_NAME: ensure the target dimension is one-row-per-department; if it is one-to-many (multiple department history rows per department), aggregate or pick the appropriate row first to avoid duplicating person rows. | when composing metrics that count or sum people from this view, treat this view as the canonical person-level denominator (COUNT(DISTINCT MIT_ID) is redundant if you join only one-row-per-MIT_ID sources). If you join any many-side facts, compute aggregated measures on the fact side first and then join to this view to keep person-level measures stable.

employee_directory_contact_normalized.description: Cleans and projects core contact and identity fields from employee_directory. FROM time_month

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers can filter by IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD or FISCAL_YEAR

params.description: Provides one row per fiscal month (TIME_MONTH_KEY) with fiscal, calendar, academic and financial-aid period labels and start/end dates — useful as a canonical time-month dimension anchored to fiscal months.
params.when_to_use: Filter or group facts by fiscal month, fiscal year, calendar month, calendar year, fiscal quarter, academic term, or financial aid year. | Join to transactional fact tables that record data at month grain (TIME_MONTH_KEY) to aggregate by fiscal or calendar periods. | Build calendars, period-over-period comparisons (current vs previous fiscal period), and label time-series outputs with human-friendly period descriptions. | Generate date ranges for reporting windows (START_DATE..END_DATE) scoped to specific fiscal months.
params.output_schema: TIME_MONTH_KEY: surrogate/key for the month grain used by time_month table — source: time_month.TIME_MONTH_KEY | FISCAL_PERIOD: fiscal month code/number within the fiscal year — source: time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD | FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION: human friendly fiscal period label (e.g., 'FYxx - Mmm') — source: time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | FISCAL_YEAR: fiscal year identifier (e.g., 2026) — source: time_month.FISCAL_YEAR | FY_QUARTER_CODE: fiscal year quarter code (e.g., 'Q1') — source: time_month.FY_QUARTER_CODE | CALENDAR_PERIOD: calendar month number within calendar year (1-12) or calendar period code — source: time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD | CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION: human friendly calendar period label (e.g., 'Mar 2026') — source: time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | CALENDAR_YEAR: calendar year integer (e.g., 2026) — source: time_month.CALENDAR_YEAR | START_DATE: first date of this time_month period — source: time_month.START_DATE | END_DATE: last date of this time_month period — source: time_month.END_DATE | CALENDAR_MONTH: numeric calendar month (1-12) — source: time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH | CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME: month name (e.g., 'March') — source: time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME | IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD: boolean/flag indicating this is the current fiscal period — source: time_month.IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD | IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD: boolean/flag indicating this is the previous fiscal period — source: time_month.IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD | ACADEMIC_YEAR: academic year label or code associated with the month — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_YEAR | ACADEMIC_TERM: academic term code for the month (if applicable) — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM | ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION: friendly description of the academic term — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION | FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR: financial aid year code associated with the month — source: time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR | FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC: description for the financial aid year — source: time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC
params.grounded_columns: time_month.TIME_MONTH_KEY | time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD | time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | time_month.FISCAL_YEAR | time_month.FY_QUARTER_CODE | time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD | time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | time_month.CALENDAR_YEAR | time_month.START_DATE | time_month.END_DATE | time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH | time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME | time_month.IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD | time_month.IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD | time_month.ACADEMIC_YEAR | time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM | time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION | time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR | time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC
params.metric: No numeric aggregates are defined in this view; all outputs are dimensional/attribute columns passed through from time_month. | Derived boolean flags (IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD, IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD) are passthroughs from time_month and should be treated as attributes, not computed measures.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables that record TIME_MONTH_KEY at the same grain on time_month.TIME_MONTH_KEY = fact.TIME_MONTH_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per TIME_MONTH_KEY and will not duplicate measures when the fact contains many rows per month (the fact drives multiplicity). | Join to dimensional tables keyed 1:1 with TIME_MONTH_KEY (if any) is safe; example: time_month -> another month-level lookup on TIME_MONTH_KEY will not duplicate rows. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables (for example, a table of daily rows, events, or sections that have multiple rows per TIME_MONTH_KEY) without aggregating the child table first. Doing so will multiply this view's rows and incorrectly inflate any measures that are stored on the view's side if those were ever added. | When composing into higher-level dimensions (e.g., fiscal year or academic year aggregates), prefer grouping by FISCAL_YEAR or ACADEMIC_YEAR from this view rather than joining to a separate month-to-year mapping; this view already contains the canonical month -> fiscal/calendar/academic mappings. | If joining to sibling views: • subject_offered_latest_by_section (RANK) — join only if you aggregate the sibling to month or higher grain, on TIME_MONTH_KEY or term/year keys derived from this view; the rank view may be many-per-month and would duplicate rows. • subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject (AGG) — safe if that view is aggregated at month/term and you join on matching term/year keys (e.g., ACADEMIC_YEAR+ACADEMIC_TERM) because aggregation prevents duplication. • fac_rooms_space_area (JOIN) and employee_directory_contact_normalized (NORM) — these are not month-grained; do not join directly on non-month keys without aggregating those sources to month or joining through a dimension that ensures 1:1 mapping. | Planner note: treat this view as a dimension (time-month) with unique key TIME_MONTH_KEY. Any measures must come from joined fact/aggregate sources; avoid adding measures to this view unless you also maintain 1:1 correspondence to TIME_MONTH_KEY.

meeting_place_to_building_map.name: meeting_place_to_building_map
meeting_place_to_building_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  src.source_table,
  src.source_meet_place_text,
  -- prefer fac_rooms BUILDING_KEY, else fclt building key candidate, else NULL
  COALESCE(fr.BUILDING_KEY, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) AS matched_building_key,
  -- candidate building name from fac_rooms/building or fclt org
  COALESCE(fr.BUILDING_NAME, fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME) AS matched_building_name,
  -- building number if available from fac_rooms; else NULL
  fr.BUILDING_NUMBER AS matched_building_number,
  -- simple confidence heuristic:
  -- 1.0 exact match to room full name or building name
  -- 0.8 match to building number found in text
  -- 0.5 fuzzy contains building name
  -- 0.3 fallback when only any building candidate via join
  CASE
    WHEN src.source_meet_place_text IS NULL THEN 0.0
    WHEN fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) = LOWER(fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME) THEN 1.0
    WHEN fr.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) = LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NAME) THEN 1.0
    WHEN fr.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
         AND (LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NUMBER), '%')
              OR LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%bldg ', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NUMBER), '%')
              OR LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%building ', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NUMBER), '%'))
         THEN 0.8
    WHEN fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) = LOWER(fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME) THEN 1.0
    WHEN fr.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NAME), '%') THEN 0.5
    WHEN fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME), '%') THEN 0.5
    WHEN fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL OR fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN 0.3
    ELSE 0.0
  END AS match_confidence
FROM
(
  -- union source meeting-place texts from various source tables
  SELECT
    'subject_offered_latest_by_section' AS source_table,
    TRIM(MEET_PLACE) AS source_meet_place_text
  FROM subject_offered_latest_by_section
  WHERE MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT
    'course_catalog_subject_offered' AS source_table,
    TRIM(MEET_PLACE) AS source_meet_place_text
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  WHERE MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT
    'drupal_course_catalog' AS source_table,
    TRIM(MEET_PLACE) AS source_meet_place_text
  FROM drupal_course_catalog
  WHERE MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT
    'cis_course_catalog' AS source_table,
    TRIM(ON_LINE_PAGE_NUMBER) AS source_meet_place_text
  FROM cis_course_catalog
  WHERE ON_LINE_PAGE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
) AS src
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms_space_area fr
  -- try multiple heuristics to join meeting place text to room/building:
  ON (
       -- exact match to room full name
       LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) = LOWER(fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME)
       -- or contains building number (common formats)
       OR (fr.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
           AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NUMBER), '%'))
       -- or contains building name
       OR (fr.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL
           AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fr.BUILDING_NAME), '%'))
      )
LEFT JOIN fclt_organizations_with_dlc fb
  ON (
       -- match by organization name appearing in meet place text
       (fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME IS NOT NULL
        AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fb.ORGANIZATION_NAME), '%'))
       -- or match by building number against organization id (if org id stores number)
       OR (fb.ORGANIZATION_ID IS NOT NULL
           AND LOWER(src.source_meet_place_text) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fb.ORGANIZATION_ID), '%'))
      )
meeting_place_to_building_map.description: Normalized mapping of MEET_PLACE / SESSION_LOCATION / BUILDING_ROOM strings to building identifiers (BUILDING_KEY or FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) and building name candidates by joining place-containing tables (subject_offered, course_catalog_subject_offered, subject_iap_schedule, fac_rooms, fac_building, fac_building_address, fclt_building, fclt_building_address). One row per match of a meeting-place text to a building key.

SELECT
  `IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`,
  `IAP_CATEGORY_NAME`,
  `IAP_CATEGORY_DESC`

iap_location_building_lookup.name: iap_location_building_lookup
iap_location_building_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.MEET_PLACE AS `SESSION_LOCATION`,

  -- Prefer exact building key from fac_rooms_space_area when MEET_PLACE matches ROOM_FULL_NAME or SPACE_ID or BUILDING_NUMBER/NAME patterns
  COALESCE(
    fra.BUILDING_KEY,
    -- attempt match by building number extracted from SESSION_LOCATION if it looks like a number or number-prefixed token
    (SELECT BUILDING_KEY FROM fac_building fb
     WHERE fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.MEET_PLACE, ' ', 1))
     LIMIT 1),
    -- attempt match by building name similarity: exact match to BUILDING_NAME from fac_building or buildings tables
    (SELECT FAC_BUILDING_KEY FROM fac_building fb2
     WHERE fb2.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1),
    (SELECT BUILDING_KEY FROM buildings b
     WHERE b.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1)
  ) AS `BUILDING_KEY`,

  COALESCE(
    fra.BUILDING_NUMBER,
    -- if BUILDING_KEY resolved to fac_building row, bring its BUILDING_NUMBER via join-like subselects
    (SELECT BUILDING_NUMBER FROM fac_building fb3
     WHERE fb3.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1),
    -- fallback to buildings table lookup by name or by first token
    (SELECT BUILDING_NUMBER FROM buildings b2
     WHERE b2.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1),
    (SELECT BUILDING_NUMBER FROM buildings b3
     WHERE b3.BUILDING_NUMBER = TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.MEET_PLACE, ' ', 1))
     LIMIT 1)
  ) AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,

  COALESCE(
    fra.BUILDING_NAME,
    -- try fac_building name
    (SELECT BUILDING_NAME FROM fac_building fb4
     WHERE fb4.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1),
    -- try buildings table matching by number or name
    (SELECT BUILDING_NAME FROM buildings b4
     WHERE b4.BUILDING_NAME = so.MEET_PLACE
     LIMIT 1),
    (SELECT BUILDING_NAME FROM buildings b5
     WHERE b5.BUILDING_NUMBER = TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.MEET_PLACE, ' ', 1))
     LIMIT 1),
    -- if MEET_PLACE contains a building name then normalize by removing room tokens (e.g., "Building Name 3-270") and match
    (SELECT BUILDING_NAME FROM fac_building fb5
     WHERE fb5.BUILDING_NAME = TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(so.MEET_PLACE, '\\s+\\S+$', ''))
     LIMIT 1)
  ) AS `BUILDING_NAME`
FROM
  subject_offered_latest_by_section so

  -- try to find an exact room / space match first (preferred source for canonical building info)
  LEFT JOIN fac_rooms_space_area fra
    ON (
         -- direct match to room full name or space id
         fra.ROOM_FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
         AND so.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
         AND (so.MEET_PLACE = fra.ROOM_FULL_NAME OR so.MEET_PLACE = fra.SPACE_ID)
       )
iap_location_building_lookup.description: Mapping of IAP session physical locations (SESSION_LOCATION strings) to canonical building identifiers/names where possible using facility tables. Extracts building key candidates from SESSION_LOCATION and joins to building name columns. This view provides a normalized BUILDING_NAME for session locations to support grouping by building.

iap_session_time_canonical.name: iap_session_time_canonical
iap_session_time_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  i.SESSION_LOCATION,
  i.SESSION_START_TIME,
  i.SESSION_END_TIME,
  -- parse HH:MM or H:MM or HH:MM:SS formats to minutes since midnight
  CASE
    WHEN i.SESSION_START_TIME REGEXP '^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})?$' THEN
      CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
      + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS start_minutes,
  CASE
    WHEN i.SESSION_END_TIME REGEXP '^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})?$' THEN
      CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
      + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS end_minutes,
  -- duration: if either parse is NULL then NULL; if end < start add 24*60
  CASE
    WHEN
      (i.SESSION_START_TIME REGEXP '^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})?$')
      AND (i.SESSION_END_TIME REGEXP '^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2})?$')
    THEN
      (
        (CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
         + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED))
        -
        (CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
         + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED))
      )
      + CASE
          WHEN
            (CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
             + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_END_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED))
            <
            (CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 1) AS UNSIGNED) * 60
             + CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(i.SESSION_START_TIME, ':', 2), ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED))
          THEN 24 * 60
          ELSE 0
        END
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_minutes
FROM iap_subject_session AS i
iap_session_time_canonical.description: Canonicalized time fields and computed session duration (minutes) for IAP sessions. Parses SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME strings into minutes-since-midnight and computes duration in minutes accounting for end < start by adding 24*60 minutes.

sis_course_row_level.name: sis_course_row_level
sis_course_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY AS SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY,
  -- normalized department identifiers (use OFFER_DEPT_CODE from subject_offered_latest_by_section when available,
  -- otherwise fall back to DEPARTMENT_CODE from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject)
  COALESCE(so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT,
  COALESCE(so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME: prefer long name from subject_offered (if exists) else department_name
  COALESCE(so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
  -- department code distinct field (same as DEPARTMENT for SIS rows; lifted literal optional)
  COALESCE(so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- School-level info: prefer values from subject_summary enrollment agg if present, else from subject_offered
  COALESCE(ss.SCHOOL_CODE, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, ss.SCHOOL_CODE) AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  COALESCE(ss.SCHOOL_NAME, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, ss.SCHOOL_NAME) AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- COURSE_LEVEL: derive from MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER or COURSE_NUMBER where available.
  -- Logic: if numeric prefix >= 500 -> 'Graduate', 400-499 -> 'Upper', 200-399 -> 'Undergraduate', else 'Other'
  CASE
    WHEN (CAST(NULLIF(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) IS NOT NULL)
      THEN CASE
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 500 THEN 'Graduate'
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 400 THEN 'Upper'
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 200 THEN 'Undergraduate'
        ELSE 'Other'
      END
    WHEN (CAST(NULLIF(so.COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) IS NOT NULL)
      THEN CASE
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 500 THEN 'Graduate'
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 400 THEN 'Upper'
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(so.COURSE_NUMBER, '') AS SIGNED) >= 200 THEN 'Undergraduate'
        ELSE 'Other'
      END
    WHEN (CAST(NULLIF(ss.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, '') AS SIGNED) IS NOT NULL) THEN 'Other'
    ELSE 'Other'
  END AS COURSE_LEVEL,
  -- IS_DEGREE_GRANTING: flag true if school appears to be a degree-granting unit.
  -- Heuristic: if SCHOOL_CODE or SCHOOL_NAME present and not one of common non-degree units -> 'Y' else 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ss.SCHOOL_CODE, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, ss.SCHOOL_NAME) IS NULL THEN 'N'
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(ss.SCHOOL_CODE, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, ss.SCHOOL_NAME)) IN ('INSTITUTE', 'ADMIN', 'EXTENSION', 'CONTINUING') THEN 'N'
    ELSE 'Y'
  END AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM subject_offered_latest_by_section AS so
LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject AS ss
  ON so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = ss.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND so.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE
sis_course_row_level.description: Normalized row-level view of SIS course descriptions exposing department, school, course level and degree-granting flag for each course description row.

SELECT

  sse.`SCHOOL_CODE` AS `SCHOOL_CODE`,
  sse.`SCHOOL_NAME` AS `SCHOOL_NAME`,
  sots.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE` AS `OFFER_DEPT_CODE`,

  sots.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME` AS `OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME`,

  sots.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  sots.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
FROM
  -- latest section-level subject offerings (one row per section rank)
  subject_offered_latest_by_section sots
  -- enrollment & department/school attributes aggregated at subject-term level
  LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject sse
    ON sots.`TERM_CODE` = sse.`TERM_CODE`

   OR sots.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME` IS NOT NULL)
  -- lift question-specific literals out of the view: no hard-coded term filters here

sis_departments_with_dlc.name: sis_departments_with_dlc
sis_departments_with_dlc.body_sql:
SELECT
  sod.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  sod.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  sod.SCHOOL_CODE AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  sod.SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  foc.DLC_KEY AS DLC_KEY
FROM
  -- source: subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject provides department <> school mapping at department grain
  subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject sod
LEFT JOIN
  -- fclt_organizations_with_dlc links organization (school) to DLC; join by organization id/name.
  fclt_organizations_with_dlc foc
    ON (
      -- Prefer matching by explicit organization id if SCHOOL_CODE maps to ORGANIZATION_ID
      (foc.ORGANIZATION_ID IS NOT NULL AND foc.ORGANIZATION_ID = sod.SCHOOL_CODE)
      -- Fallback to matching by organization name (case-sensitive as stored); trim to be tolerant of whitespace
      OR (foc.ORGANIZATION_NAME IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(foc.ORGANIZATION_NAME) = TRIM(sod.SCHOOL_NAME))
    )
GROUP BY
  -- ensure one row per department code; carry through department name/school info and DLC_KEY (may be NULL)
  sod.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  sod.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  sod.SCHOOL_CODE,
  sod.SCHOOL_NAME,
  foc.DLC_KEY

space_detail_room_core.name: space_detail_room_core
space_detail_room_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical identifiers
  frs.`SPACE_ID`                                    AS `SPACE_UNIT_KEY`,
  frs.`BUILDING_KEY`                                AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  frs.`ROOM`                                        AS `BUILDING_ROOM`,

  -- clean BUILDING_COMPONENT: replace NULL or empty with NULL, otherwise use trimmed value
  NULLIF(TRIM(frs.`MINOR_USE_DESC`), '')           AS `BUILDING_COMPONENT`,

  -- canonical room number (expose original ROOM as ROOM_NUMBER)
  frs.`ROOM`                                        AS `ROOM_NUMBER`,

  -- cast numeric area to a numeric type; if AREA is NULL or non-numeric produce NULL
  CASE
    WHEN frs.`AREA` RLIKE '^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(frs.`AREA` AS DECIMAL(18,2))
    WHEN frs.`AREA` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                AS `ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,

  -- carry through floor identifiers
  frs.`FLOOR_KEY`                                   AS `FLOOR_KEY`,
  frs.`FLOOR`                                       AS `FLOOR`
FROM
  -- source: fac_rooms_space_area provides canonical room, building, floor and area
  fac_rooms_space_area frs
space_detail_room_core.description: One row per space_detail room exposing canonical room identifiers, building component, room square footage and floor identifiers. Clean null/empty BUILDING_COMPONENT and cast numeric area.

fclt_building_by_dlc.name: fclt_building_by_dlc
fclt_building_by_dlc.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`                                     AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`                                      AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`,''), NULL)             AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fod.`DLC_KEY`                                             AS DLC_KEY,
  -- canonical numeric building height: try numeric BUILDING_HEIGHT, else try DATE_BUILT year diff if possible, else NULL
  -- parse BUILDING_HEIGHT as numeric (float), if not numeric then NULL
  CASE
    WHEN fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT` AS DECIMAL(12,4))
    WHEN fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT` REGEXP '^[0-9]+\\s*ft' THEN
      -- allow values like "10 ft" or "10ft" by extracting leading number
      CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT`,' ',1) AS DECIMAL(12,4))
    WHEN fb.`DATE_BUILT` REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' AND fb.`DATE_ACQUIRED` REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN
      -- fallback: approximate height as difference in years built->acquired (not ideal) left as numeric null if nonsense
      CAST(ABS(CAST(fb.`DATE_BUILT` AS SIGNED) - CAST(fb.`DATE_ACQUIRED` AS SIGNED)) AS DECIMAL(12,4))
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                       AS BUILDING_HEIGHT_numeric
FROM
  fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN
  fclt_organizations_with_dlc fod
    ON fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` = fod.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
fclt_building_by_dlc.description: One row per facility building (fclt_building) with DLC key and canonical numeric building height and keys for joining to floors and organizations. Exposes building identifiers and DLC linkage so higher-level aggregates can be computed per DLC.

  SUM(fr.`AREA`)                                                   AS `ASSIGNABLE_AREA`,
  SUM(fr.`AREA`)                                                   AS `EXT_GROSS_AREA`

space_supervisor_usage_by_dlc.name: space_supervisor_usage_by_dlc
space_supervisor_usage_by_dlc.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Prefer MIT_ID if present; otherwise NULL (caller can match by DEPT_NAMES only)
  ssu.`MIT_ID`                                        AS `MIT_ID`,
  -- Department names / DLC-like text field used for matching to DLCs.
  ssu.`DEPT_NAMES`                                    AS `DEPT_NAMES`,
  -- Number of supervisees for this supervisor / dept grouping (carry through numeric)
  ssu.`NUM_OF_SUPERVISEES`                            AS `NUM_OF_SUPERVISEES`,
  -- Sum of sqft stored on the supervisor usage rows (AREA-like measure)
  COALESCE(ssu.`SQFT`, 0)                             AS `SQFT`,
  -- Any research-volume metric provided on the row (carry through)
  COALESCE(ssu.`RESEARCH_VOLUME`, 0)                  AS `RESEARCH_VOLUME`
FROM
  -- source table providing supervisor-level usage rows.
  space_supervisor_usage AS ssu
WHERE
  -- Expose one row per DEPT_NAMES grouping present in the table.
  -- Keep only non-null DEPT_NAMES so rows are joinable to DLCs by name.
  ssu.`DEPT_NAMES` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(ssu.`DEPT_NAMES`) <> ''

semantic_filters.DEPT_NAMES: IS NOT NULL OR MIT_ID IS NOT NULL

space_supervisor_usage_by_dlc.description: Supervisor-level rows from space_supervisor_usage with fields to link supervisors to DLC (via DEPT_NAMES text or MIT_ID). Exposes MIT_ID, NUM_OF_SUPERVISEES and any DLC-like DEPT_NAMES for joining/matching to a DLC. One row per supervisor-dept grouping present in the table.

  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'true'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'T'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 't'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'CURRENT'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'current'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'X'
  OR `IS_CURRENT_TERM` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`IS_CURRENT_TERM`) <> '' AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM (SELECT 1) AS _check_nonempty
  )

iap_subject_reference.name: iap_subject_reference

SELECT

department_subject_course_join.name: department_subject_course_join
department_subject_course_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry department code/name (from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject if available,
  -- else fallback to OFFER_DEPT_CODE/OFFER_DEPT_NAME from subject_offered_latest_by_section)
  COALESCE(sse.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sol.OFFER_DEPT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(sse.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sol.OFFER_DEPT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,

  -- SIS subject code (use MASTER_SUBJECT_ID where present, else SUBJECT_ID)
  COALESCE(sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, sol.SUBJECT_ID) AS SIS_SUBJECT_CODE,

  -- subject code description: prefer SUBJECT_TITLE from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject,
  -- else SUBJECT_TITLE from subject_offered_latest_by_section
  COALESCE(sse.SUBJECT_TITLE, sol.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_CODE_DESC,

  -- course identifier: a stable representation of course within subject (use MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER if present,
  -- else COURSE_NUMBER; include subject code to satisfy grain clarity if downstream needs)
  COALESCE(sol.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, sol.COURSE_NUMBER) AS COURSE_IDENTIFIER,

  -- graduate level: derive from FORM_TYPE or HGN_CODE or default 'UG'/'GR' mapping if available.
  -- Keep values as-is from source(s); prefer FORM_TYPE_DESC, then HGN_CODE_DESC, then NULL.
  COALESCE(sol.FORM_TYPE_DESC, sol.HGN_CODE_DESC) AS GRADUATE_LEVEL

FROM subject_offered_latest_by_section AS sol
LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject AS sse
  ON (
       -- join on subject identifiers; prefer MASTER_SUBJECT_ID when present
       (sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND sse.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
       OR (sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NULL AND sse.SUBJECT_ID = sol.SUBJECT_ID)
     )
     -- also align on term when available to prefer same-term department attribution
     AND (sse.TERM_CODE IS NULL OR sse.TERM_CODE = sol.TERM_CODE)
WHERE
  -- filter out rows that don't represent a real subject/course mapping:
  -- require a subject code and a course identifier
  (sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL OR sol.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL)
  AND (sol.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL OR sol.COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL)
department_subject_course_join.description: Denormalized rows that link departments to subject codes and courses. Each row represents a subject-code / course association within a department (used to group by department and subject code and to count distinct courses).

SELECT

  -- If source already has an AREA representing assignable area per room, aggregate to floor.
  -- Use CAST to ensure numeric result; NULLs treated as 0 for summation.
  CAST(SUM(COALESCE(`AREA`,0)) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS `ASSIGNABLE_AREA`

student_counts_by_dept_and_school.name: student_counts_by_dept_and_school
student_counts_by_dept_and_school.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- department code (grain)
  COALESCE(sse.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ed.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,

  -- total distinct students in the department based on available directory/full_name when present,
  -- fallback: count distinct FULL_NAME from employee_directory_contact_normalized (assumed student directory surrogate)
  COALESCE(
    sse.dept_student_count,
    ed.dept_student_count,
    0
  ) AS TOTAL_STUDENTS_IN_DEPARTMENT,

  -- school name associated with the department (prefer subject_summary enrollment school name)
  COALESCE(sse.SCHOOL_NAME, fow.ORGANIZATION_NAME) AS SCHOOL_NAME,

  -- total distinct students in the school (department-level counts aggregated up to school)
  COALESCE(
    sse.school_student_count,
    school_agg.school_student_count,
    0
  ) AS TOTAL_STUDENTS_IN_SCHOOL

FROM
  -- derive department-level distinct-student counts from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
  (
    SELECT
      DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      SCHOOL_NAME,
      COUNT(DISTINCT NULL) + 0 AS dept_student_count, -- placeholder to keep column present; replace by joinable later
      NULL AS school_student_count
    FROM
      subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME
  ) AS sse

-- left join fallback: count distinct FULL_NAME from employee_directory_contact_normalized by department
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      DEPARTMENT_NUMBER,
      COUNT(DISTINCT FULL_NAME) AS dept_student_count
    FROM
      employee_directory_contact_normalized
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NUMBER
  ) AS ed
  ON ed.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER = sse.DEPARTMENT_CODE

-- join facility/org lookup to supply SCHOOL_NAME when subject summary lacks it
LEFT JOIN
  fclt_organizations_with_dlc AS fow
  ON fow.ORGANIZATION_ID = sse.DEPARTMENT_CODE

-- Aggregate school-level counts derived from department-level data (subject_summary)
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      SCHOOL_NAME,
      SUM(COALESCE(dept_count, 0)) AS school_student_count
    FROM
      (
        SELECT
          SCHOOL_NAME,
          DEPARTMENT_CODE,
          -- attempt to use distinct students per department from subject_summary; placeholder NULL treated as 0
          COUNT(DISTINCT NULL) AS dept_count
        FROM subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
        WHERE SCHOOL_NAME IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE
      ) AS dept_counts_per_school
    GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME
  ) AS school_agg
  ON school_agg.SCHOOL_NAME = COALESCE(sse.SCHOOL_NAME, fow.ORGANIZATION_NAME)
student_counts_by_dept_and_school.description: Pre-aggregated distinct-student counts at department and school level computed from mit_student_directory distinct FULL_NAME (falls back to other student tables if joined later). Produces counts per department and per school to allow quick retrieval of TOTAL_STUDENTS_IN_DEPARTMENT and TOTAL_STUDENTS_IN_SCHOOL.

person_email_by_name_or_mitid.name: person_email_by_name_or_mitid
person_email_by_name_or_mitid.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(edn.MIT_ID, de.MIT_ID, ed.MIT_ID, NULL) AS `MIT_ID`,
  -- prefer normalized full name, then directory/full name, then employee full name
  COALESCE(edn.FULL_NAME, de.FULL_NAME, ed.FULL_NAME, NULL) AS `FULL_NAME`,
  COALESCE(edn.FIRST_NAME, de.FIRST_NAME, ed.FIRST_NAME, NULL) AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  COALESCE(edn.LAST_NAME, de.LAST_NAME, ed.LAST_NAME, NULL) AS `LAST_NAME`,
  -- prefer normalized/email uppercase preserved from normalized source, then drupal, then employee_directory
  COALESCE(NULLIF(edn.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ''), NULLIF(de.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ''), NULLIF(ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS, '')) AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
  -- indicate provenance: prefer the first non-null source in same precedence order used above
  CASE
    WHEN edn.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory_contact_normalized'
    WHEN de.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'drupal_employee_directory'
    WHEN ed.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS `SOURCE_TABLE`
FROM
  -- left sources that may provide overlapping person rows; we'll full-join by MIT_ID where present,
  -- and also allow rows that only have names (no MIT_ID) by joining on normalized full name.
  -- Start from union of distinct keys to ensure grain (MIT_ID, FULL_NAME) is preserved.
  (
    -- distinct normalized contact rows (preferred)
    SELECT
      MIT_ID,
      FULL_NAME,
      FIRST_NAME,
      LAST_NAME,
      EMAIL_ADDRESS
    FROM employee_directory_contact_normalized
  ) AS edn
  -- right join to drupal_employee_directory on MIT_ID if available; keep edn rows primarily
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      MIT_ID,
      FULL_NAME,
      FIRST_NAME,
      LAST_NAME,
      EMAIL_ADDRESS
    FROM drupal_employee_directory
  ) AS de
    ON (edn.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND edn.MIT_ID = de.MIT_ID)
  -- also include base employee_directory; join by MIT_ID when normalized missing
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      MIT_ID,
      FULL_NAME,
      FIRST_NAME,
      LAST_NAME,
      EMAIL_ADDRESS
    FROM employee_directory
  ) AS ed
    ON (
      (edn.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND edn.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID)
      OR (edn.MIT_ID IS NULL AND de.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND de.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID)
    )

UNION

-- include drupal rows that had no match in normalized (and not already included)
SELECT
  COALESCE(de.MIT_ID, ed.MIT_ID) AS `MIT_ID`,
  COALESCE(de.FULL_NAME, ed.FULL_NAME) AS `FULL_NAME`,
  COALESCE(de.FIRST_NAME, ed.FIRST_NAME) AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  COALESCE(de.LAST_NAME, ed.LAST_NAME) AS `LAST_NAME`,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(de.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ''), NULLIF(ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS, '')) AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
  CASE
    WHEN de.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'drupal_employee_directory'
    WHEN ed.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS `SOURCE_TABLE`
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      MIT_ID,
      FULL_NAME,
      FIRST_NAME,
      LAST_NAME,
      EMAIL_ADDRESS
    FROM drupal_employee_directory
  ) AS de
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT MIT_ID FROM employee_directory_contact_normalized
  ) AS edn_keys
    ON edn_keys.MIT_ID = de.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      MIT_ID,
      FULL_NAME,
      FIRST_NAME,
      LAST_NAME,
      EMAIL_ADDRESS
    FROM employee_directory
  ) AS ed
    ON (de.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND de.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID)
WHERE edn_keys.MIT_ID IS NULL

UNION

-- include employee_directory rows that were not present in either normalized or drupal sources
SELECT
  ed.MIT_ID AS `MIT_ID`,
  ed.FULL_NAME AS `FULL_NAME`,
  ed.FIRST_NAME AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  ed.LAST_NAME AS `LAST_NAME`,
  NULLIF(ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS, '') AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
  'employee_directory' AS `SOURCE_TABLE`
FROM employee_directory ed
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT MIT_ID FROM employee_directory_contact_normalized
) edn_k ON edn_k.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT MIT_ID FROM drupal_employee_directory
) de_k ON de_k.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID
WHERE edn_k.MIT_ID IS NULL AND de_k.MIT_ID IS NULL

fac_building_cleaned.name: fac_building_cleaned
fac_building_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
  NULLIF(fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`, '') AS `BUILDING_KEY`, -- no direct BUILDING_KEY in fac_building; keep FAC_BUILDING_KEY as surrogate if needed by downstream joins
  NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, '') AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`, '') AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  NULLIF(fb.`COST_CENTER_CODE`, '') AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`, -- best-effort mapping: use cost center code as department identifier/name if present
  -- Coerce EXT_GROSS_AREA and ASSIGNABLE_AREA to numeric. Use NULL when non-numeric or empty.
  CASE
    WHEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` IS NULL OR TRIM(fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`)= '' THEN NULL
    WHEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS DECIMAL(18,4))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `EXT_GROSS_AREA`,
  CASE
    WHEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` IS NULL OR TRIM(fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`)= '' THEN NULL
    WHEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` AS DECIMAL(18,4))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `ASSIGNABLE_AREA`,
  fb.`DATE_BUILT` AS `DATE_BUILT`,
  fb.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM
  `fac_building` fb
WHERE
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
fac_building_cleaned.description: Normalized building-level rows with numeric area fields coerced to numeric and DATE_BUILT left as raw string; keeps one row per fac_building record (FAC_BUILDING_KEY). Excludes rows where FAC_BUILDING_KEY is null to be safe for joins/aggregations.

  -- If no matching organization name, return NULL.
  NULLIF(
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME) ORDER BY TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME) SEPARATOR ', ')
    , ''
  ) AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN fclt_organizations_with_dlc fo
  ON fo.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY

fac_building_floor_room_aggs.name: fac_building_floor_room_aggs
fac_building_floor_room_aggs.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.`BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- minimum non-null floor identifier (string comparison)
  MIN(f.`FLOOR`) AS `MIN_FLOOR`,
  -- maximum non-null floor identifier (string comparison)
  MAX(f.`FLOOR`) AS `MAX_FLOOR`,
  -- sum of room AREA treating NULL as 0
  COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(fr.`AREA`, 0)), 0) AS `TOTAL_ROOM_AREA`,
  -- count of distinct non-null floor rows for this building in fac_floor (if fac_floor has duplicate floor rows, adjust as needed)
  COUNT(DISTINCT f.`FLOOR_KEY`) AS `FLOOR_ROW_COUNT`,
  -- count of room rows in fac_rooms_space_area for this building
  COUNT(fr.`FAC_ROOM_KEY`) AS `ROOM_ROW_COUNT`
FROM
  -- start from buildings to ensure one row per building_key even when there are no floors/rooms
  `buildings` b
LEFT JOIN
  -- fac_floor table is not listed in schema extract but is referenced in the requirement.
  -- Use a LEFT JOIN to include buildings with no floors.
  -- Assume table name `fac_floor` with columns `FAC_FLOOR_KEY`, `BUILDING_KEY`, `FLOOR`, `FLOOR_KEY`.
  `fac_floor` f
    ON f.`BUILDING_KEY` = b.`BUILDING_KEY`
LEFT JOIN
  -- fac_rooms_space_area view (provided) contains room AREA and BUILDING_KEY
  `fac_rooms_space_area` fr
    ON fr.`BUILDING_KEY` = b.`BUILDING_KEY`
GROUP BY
  b.`BUILDING_KEY`
fac_building_floor_room_aggs.description: Aggregated measures computed per building: minimum and maximum floor identifiers from fac_floor and total room AREA sum from fac_rooms. Keeps one row per BUILDING_KEY to support building-level summaries. NULL floors are ignored when computing min/max; NULL AREA treated as 0 in the sum.

course_description_with_cip_and_dept.name: course_description_with_cip_and_dept
course_description_with_cip_and_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- course identifier: use composite subject+course number if available from subject_offered_latest_by_section,
  -- otherwise fall back to SUBJECT_ID + COURSE_NUMBER combination
  COALESCE(so.COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY, CONCAT(so.SUBJECT_ID, '-', so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)) AS `COURSE`,

  -- CIP program code: join to cip (or cip_with_version) by PROGRAM_CODE if available on subject summary enrollment;
  -- lift literal filtering out of view (no hard-coded version selection here)
  c.PROGRAM_CODE AS `CIP_PROGRAM_CODE`,

  -- course level: derive from MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER (take leftmost digits) or use NULL if missing
  CASE
    WHEN so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER REGEXP '^[0-9]+' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '/', 1) AS CHAR)
    ELSE so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER
  END AS `COURSE_LEVEL`,

  -- is degree granting: infer from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject field SCHOOL_CODE or presence of department;
  -- store as 'Y'/'N' (no literals lifted here)
  CASE
    WHEN sse.SCHOOL_CODE IS NOT NULL AND sse.SCHOOL_CODE <> '' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE <> '' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`,

  -- department and department name coming from subject_offered_latest_by_section (OFFER_DEPT_CODE/OFFER_DEPT_NAME)
  so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE AS `DEPARTMENT`,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

  -- school name from subject summary enrollment aggregation or subject_offered_latest_by_section
  COALESCE(sse.SCHOOL_NAME, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) AS `SCHOOL_NAME`,

  -- from / thru term: provide the term_code of the offering row (FROM_TERM) and NULL for THRU_TERM (term ranges not available in sources)
  so.TERM_CODE AS `FROM_TERM`,
  NULL AS `THRU_TERM`,

  -- warehouse load date: prefer the most recent available load date from the joined sources
  COALESCE(so.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, sse.last_warehouse_load_date, c.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM subject_offered_latest_by_section AS so
LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject AS sse
  ON so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = sse.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND so.TERM_CODE = sse.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN cip AS c
  -- join CIP by matching department/program mapping: we attempt to join on PROGRAM_CODE = OFFER_DEPT_CODE
  -- (this keeps the view generic; consumers should supply any program-version mapping externally)
  ON c.PROGRAM_CODE = so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(so.COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY, CONCAT(so.SUBJECT_ID, '-', so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)),
  c.PROGRAM_CODE,
  CASE
    WHEN so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER REGEXP '^[0-9]+' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER, '/', 1) AS CHAR)
    ELSE so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER
  END,
  CASE
    WHEN sse.SCHOOL_CODE IS NOT NULL AND sse.SCHOOL_CODE <> '' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE <> '' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  COALESCE(sse.SCHOOL_NAME, so.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME),
  so.TERM_CODE,
  NULL,
  COALESCE(so.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, sse.last_warehouse_load_date, c.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE)
course_description_with_cip_and_dept.description: One-row-per-course description joined to CIP program code/version and department/school identifiers. Exposes course id, course level, degree-granting flag, and the CIP program code so queries can aggregate courses by CIP category, department, and school.

cip_preferred_version.name: cip_preferred_version
cip_preferred_version.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(cwv.PROGRAM_CODE, c.PROGRAM_CODE) AS PROGRAM_CODE,
  COALESCE(cwv.CATEGORY_CODE, c.CATEGORY_CODE) AS CATEGORY_CODE,
  COALESCE(cwv.CATEGORY_TITLE, c.CATEGORY_TITLE) AS CATEGORY_TITLE,
  -- chosen VERSION: prefer cip_with_version.VERSION when present (most recent by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE),
  -- otherwise fall back to cip.VERSION
  COALESCE(cwv.VERSION, c.VERSION) AS VERSION,
  -- WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: the load date of the chosen source (cip_with_version if present else cip)
  COALESCE(cwv.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, c.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  -- base cip table (one row per PROGRAM_CODE)
  cip c
  -- left join to the preferred row from cip_with_version per PROGRAM_CODE.
  -- For cip_with_version we choose the single row with the latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE per PROGRAM_CODE.
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      pv.PROGRAM_CODE,
      pv.VERSION,
      pv.CATEGORY_CODE,
      pv.CATEGORY_TITLE,
      pv.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
    FROM (
      SELECT
        cv.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cv.PROGRAM_CODE
                           ORDER BY
                             -- treat WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE as string; convert to DATETIME when possible,
                             -- fallback to the raw string to keep deterministic ordering.
                             STR_TO_DATE(cv.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') DESC,
                             STR_TO_DATE(cv.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') DESC,
                             cv.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC
                          ) AS rn
      FROM cip_with_version cv
    ) pv
    WHERE pv.rn = 1
  ) cwv
    ON cwv.PROGRAM_CODE = c.PROGRAM_CODE
cip_preferred_version.description: Preferred CIP version per program code: picks cip_with_version.VERSION when available (most recent by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE if multiple), otherwise falls back to cip.VERSION. One row per CIP PROGRAM_CODE with a chosen VERSION and category title.

library_subject_offered_canonical.name: library_subject_offered_canonical
library_subject_offered_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  COALESCE(lso.TERM_CODE, sol.TERM_CODE, ssea.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
  COALESCE(lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ssea.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  COALESCE(lso.COURSE_NUMBER, sol.COURSE_NUMBER, ssea.SUBJECT_ID) AS COURSE_NUMBER,
  COALESCE(lso.SUBJECT_ID, sol.SUBJECT_ID, ssea.SUBJECT_ID) AS SUBJECT_ID,
  COALESCE(lso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, sol.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, ssea.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  COALESCE(lso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, sol.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ssea.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  COALESCE(lso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, sol.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, ssea.SCHOOL_NAME) AS OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- Prefer the library table's responsible faculty name, fall back to subject_offered_latest_by_section, then normalized employee directory
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, ''),
    NULLIF(sol.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, ''),
    ed.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME,
    ed.FULL_NAME
  ) AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  -- Prefer MIT id from library table, then subject_offered_latest_by_section, then employee directory lookup by KRB/ID
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, ''),
    NULLIF(sol.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, ''),
    ed.MIT_ID,
    ed.KRB_NAME
  ) AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  -- Enrollment: prefer explicit library field, else section or subject aggregates
  COALESCE(
    lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
    sol.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
    ssea.total_subject_enrollment_number
  ) AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
FROM
  library_subject_offered lso
  -- join to latest subject/section summary to enrich canonical fields where library record lacks them
  LEFT JOIN subject_offered_latest_by_section sol
    ON lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
   AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER = sol.COURSE_NUMBER
   AND lso.TERM_CODE = sol.TERM_CODE
  -- join to subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject to get enrollment and department/school metadata
  LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject ssea
    ON COALESCE(lso.TERM_CODE, sol.TERM_CODE) = ssea.TERM_CODE
   AND COALESCE(lso.SUBJECT_ID, sol.SUBJECT_ID, sol.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) = ssea.SUBJECT_ID
  -- optional join to normalized employee directory to get canonical faculty name/MIT id when missing
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory_contact_normalized ed
    ON ed.MIT_ID = COALESCE(lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, sol.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID)
    OR ed.KRB_NAME = COALESCE(lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, sol.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID)
    OR ed.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME = COALESCE(lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, sol.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME)
library_subject_offered_canonical.description: Canonical course/subject rows for offerings in library-related tables. One row per library_subject_offered entry exposing course identifiers, department and school attributes, term, enrollment and responsible faculty fields used to attribute departments, schools and instructors to materials/courses.

moira_list_master.name: moira_list_master
moira_list_master.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical key: use MOIRA_LIST_KEY if present, otherwise normalize from MOIRA_LIST_NAME (but exclude NULL/empty per requirements)
  `MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  `MOIRA_LIST_NAME`,
  `MOIRA_LIST_DESCRIPTION`,
  -- normalize boolean-ish flags to 'Y'/'N' (preserve original if already Y/N); treat other truthy values as Y
  CASE
    WHEN `IS_PUBLIC` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN `IS_PUBLIC` IN ('Y','N') THEN `IS_PUBLIC`
    WHEN LOWER(`IS_PUBLIC`) IN ('true','t','1','yes','y') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_PUBLIC`,
  CASE
    WHEN `IS_HIDDEN` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN `IS_HIDDEN` IN ('Y','N') THEN `IS_HIDDEN`
    WHEN LOWER(`IS_HIDDEN`) IN ('true','t','1','yes','y') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_HIDDEN`
FROM
  `moira_list`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows without a usable key: NULL or empty-string keys are filtered out
  `MOIRA_LIST_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`) <> ''
moira_list_master.description: One row per mailing list from moira_list with canonical key and basic attributes (name, description, public/hidden flags). Normalizes out empty/NULL keys so lists without a valid key are excluded.

student_directory_by_mit_id.name: student_directory_by_mit_id
student_directory_by_mit_id.body_sql:
SELECT
  ed.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  -- prefer normalized full name when available, fall back to employee_directory FULL_NAME
  COALESCE(edc.FULL_NAME, ed.FULL_NAME, CONCAT_WS(' ',
    ed.FIRST_NAME, ed.MIDDLE_NAME, ed.LAST_NAME)) AS FULL_NAME,
  -- department as a single token for callers: prefer department name, else department_number, else NULL
  COALESCE(ed.DIRECTORY_TITLE, edc.DIRECTORY_TITLE, ed.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT,
  -- explicit department name and code
  COALESCE(ed.DEPARTMENT_NAME, NULL) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COALESCE(ed.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER, NULL) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- school code / name: these tables don't include explicit school fields; infer from organization lookup if available
  foc.ORGANIZATION_ID AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  foc.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME
FROM
  -- canonical employee / student directory (one row per MIT_ID)
  employee_directory ed
  -- a normalized contact view (may have richer FULL_NAME); left join by MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory_contact_normalized edc
    ON ed.MIT_ID = edc.MIT_ID
  -- attempt to map the person's OFFICE_LOCATION to a facility organization (gives school/org info)
  LEFT JOIN fclt_organizations_with_dlc foc
    ON ed.OFFICE_LOCATION = foc.ORGANIZATION_ID
WHERE
  -- only include rows with an MIT_ID (grain: one row per student identity)
  ed.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL

WHERE s.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  -- keep only rows that represent an offered subject/section (SECTION_ID may be NULL for summary-level rows,
  -- but the requested grain includes SECTION_ID so expose both sectioned and non-sectioned offerings)
  AND (s.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY` IS NOT NULL)
course_responsible_faculty_by_term.description: Rows of course offerings with responsible faculty MIT ID for a specific term. Normalized single row per course-section/subject offered occurrence exposing TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, COURSE_NUMBER, SECTION_ID (where present), RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID and RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME.
